hero.title: Incentive plans: phantom shares and stock options connected to the shareholder register
hero.description: Sttok manages each plan from the pool approved by the general meeting through to liquidity: grants, vesting, invitation letters and the beneficiary portal. Units are calculated on the actual capital in the shareholder register.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about incentive plans

items.a: Phantom shares, stock options and restricted shares. Each plan has its instrument, its conditions and its exercise price.
Their granted units, what has vested, the next tranche, their documents and, if a window is open, what they can sell.
Each grant has its letter. The company sees which are accepted and which are pending, and pending units do not vest until the letter is accepted.

items.q: Does it calculate the plan's dilution?
items.a: Yes. It shows the pool over fully diluted capital and the granted units over the pool, using the actual shareholder register.

items.q: Does it work for family businesses and groups?
items.a: Yes. Management plans work the same way: a pool approved by the general meeting, grants, vesting and liquidity.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.

situations.title: Common situations in an incentive plan

rows.situation: The general meeting approves a larger pool
rows.action: The resolution is recorded and the plan's available units are updated.

rows.situation: A new executive joins with a plan
rows.action: The grant is created, the invitation letter is prepared and the vesting schedule starts.

rows.situation: An employee asks how much has vested
rows.action: They see it in their portal: what has vested, what is pending and the date of the next tranche.
Units that have not vested return to the plan's pool.

rows.situation: The company opens a liquidity window
rows.action: Price, cap, withholding and net amount are calculated for each beneficiary.
Every settlement keeps a record of its withholding.
